name: Synthetic sensor anomaly detection on IBM Cloud

data.label: Synthetic device publisher
data.description: An external test publisher sends synthetic telemetry: device_id, event_id, timestamp, value and unit. It sits outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Telemetry buffer
data.description: A Kafka topic (telemetry.raw) keyed by device_id keeps order per device. Retention allows replay after a disconnect, and consumers resume from committed offsets. A telemetry.rejected topic holds invalid events with a reason.

data.label: Validator & scoring app
data.description: Consumer app. It rejects unknown devices and invalid units, keeping device identity, timestamps and units unchanged. It drops duplicates by device_id + event_id and applies the explicit late/out-of-order window. It then calls the model, writes an idempotent result and raises alerts.

data.label: Device registry
data.description: Lists known device IDs and the units allowed for each sensor. It is read by the validator.

data.label: Anomaly model
data.description: Deployed anomaly model that returns a score, evidence features and a model version. It is mocked in the local test, and its real quality is unvalidated.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: Stores results with a unique key (device_id, event_id), so a duplicate event gives one result. Each result records the evidence and model version.

data.label: Operator alert
data.description: Sends anomaly alerts that name the device, evidence and model version to the operator destination.

data.label: Operator
data.description: The person who receives and triages anomaly alerts.

data.label: Pipeline monitoring
data.description: Tracks consumer lag, reject counts, duplicates dropped, late events and model latency.

brief.application: Use IBM Cloud for this synthetic architecture qualification. Analyze synthetic sensor events for anomalous device behavior. Preserve device identity, timestamps and units. Include ingestion, durable buffering, validation, inference, results and an operator alert. Acceptance criteria: Reject unknown device and invalid units; Duplicate events produce one result; Late and out-of-order telemetry follows an explicit policy; Disconnected input recovers by replay; Anomaly output names evidence and model version. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

decisions.subject: design.ibm-sensor-anomaly-pipeline-first-concrete-sketch
decisions.title: IBM sensor anomaly pipeline – first concrete sketch
decisions.context: Scope: synthetic sensor events through ingestion, durable buffering, validation, inference, results and operator alerting on IBM Cloud. Assumptions: the region is still to be selected, and the model is mocked in the local test and remains unvalidated. Event Streams keeps raw topics for replay and a reject topic for failed events. Neither IBM Terraform generation nor any deployment is covered or verified.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: Events from unknown devices or with invalid units are rejected with a reason and never scored.
needs.rationale: Stops bad data from producing false anomalies.
needs.basis: User: "Reject unknown device and invalid units"

needs.statement: Duplicate events (same device_id and event_id) produce exactly one result.
needs.rationale: Prevents repeated alerts and double counting.

needs.statement: Late and out-of-order telemetry is handled by an explicit, documented window. The window length is still open.
needs.rationale: Without a policy, results can't be reproduced.
needs.basis: User: "Late and out-of-order telemetry follows an explicit policy"

needs.statement: After a disconnect, processing resumes by replaying from committed Event Streams offsets without losing events.
needs.rationale: Ensures recovery doesn't lose data or create duplicates.

needs.statement: Each anomaly result and alert names its evidence and model version, and preserves device identity, timestamps and units.
needs.rationale: Lets operators audit and trust alerts.
needs.basis: User: "Anomaly output names evidence and model version"
